sentences.en: YOUNG MAN: That seminar yesterday on automation and the future of work was really good, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 年轻男子：昨天那场关于自动化与未来工作的研讨会真的很棒，不是吗？

sentences.en: Looking at the first industrial revolution in Britain in the 19th century and seeing how people reacted to massive change was a real eye-opener
sentences.zh: 回顾19世纪英国第一次工业革命时期人们面对巨变时的反应，真是令人眼界大开。

sentences.en: YOUNG WOMAN: Yes
sentences.zh: 年轻女子：是的。

sentences.en: It was interesting to hear how people felt about automation then and what challenges they faced
sentences.zh: 听到当时人们对自动化的感受以及他们所面临的挑战，很有意思。

sentences.en: I didn't know that first started with workers in the textile industry
sentences.zh: 我以前不知道自动化最初是从纺织业工人开始的。

sentences.en: YOUNG MAN: With those protesting workers called the Luddites destroying their knitting machines because they were so worried about losing their jobs
sentences.zh: 年轻男子：那些抗议的工人被称为‘卢德分子’，他们因极度担忧失业而砸毁了针织机。

sentences.en: YOUNG WOMAN: Yes, and ultimately, they didn't achieve anything
sentences.zh: 年轻女子：是的，而且最终他们什么也没达成。

sentences.en: And anyway, /22 industrialisation created more jobs than it destroyed
sentences.zh: 况且，工业化创造的就业岗位比它摧毁的还要多。

sentences.en: YOUNG MAN: Yes, that's true - but it probably didn't seem a positive thing at the time
sentences.zh: 年轻男子：没错——但当时这很可能并不显得是件积极的事。

sentences.en: I can /22 see why the Luddites felt so threatened
sentences.zh: 我能理解卢德分子为何感到如此受威胁。

sentences.en: YOUNG WOMAN: know
sentences.zh: 年轻女子：知道。

sentences.en: I'm sure I would have felt the same
sentences.zh: 我确信我也会有同样的感受。

sentences.en: The discussion about the future of work was really optimistic for a change
sentences.zh: 关于未来工作的讨论这次出人意料地非常乐观。

sentences.en: I like the idea that work won't involve doing boring, repetitive tasks, as robots will do all that
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这种设想：工作将不再包含枯燥、重复的任务，因为这些都将由机器人来完成。

sentences.en: Normally, you only hear negative stuff about the future
sentences.zh: 通常，你只能听到有关未来的负面消息。

sentences.en: YOUNG MAN: Bit too optimistic, don't you think?
sentences.zh: 年轻男子：是不是有点过于乐观了？你不这么认为吗？

sentences.en: For example, I can't see how people are about to have more leisure time, when all the evidence shows people are /24 spending longer than ever at work
sentences.zh: 例如，我看不出人们怎么可能会拥有更多闲暇时间，因为所有证据都表明，人们目前的工作时间比以往任何时候都更长。

sentences.en: YOUNG WOMAN: No - that's true
sentences.zh: 年轻女子：不——这倒是真的。

sentences.en: And what about lower unemployment?
sentences.zh: 那失业率降低呢？

sentences.en: I'm not so sure about that. /24
sentences.zh: 我对这一点不太确定。

sentences.en: YOUNG MAN: Perhaps in the long term - but not in the foreseeable future
sentences.zh: 年轻男子：或许从长远来看会如此——但在可预见的将来则未必。

sentences.en: YOUNG WOMAN: Mmm
sentences.zh: YOUNG WOMAN: 嗯。

sentences.en: And expect most people will be expected to work until they're much older - as everyone's living much longer
sentences.zh: 而且，由于人们的寿命普遍延长，大多数人恐怕将被期望工作到更年长的年纪。

sentences.en: YOUNG MAN: That's already happening
sentences.zh: 年轻男子：这已经发生了。

sentences.en: YOUNG WOMAN: I enjoyed all that stuff on how technology has changed some jobs and how they're likely to change in the near future
sentences.zh: 年轻女子：我很喜欢那些关于技术如何改变某些职业，以及这些职业在不久的将来可能如何变化的内容。

sentences.en: YOUNG MAN: Yeah, incredible
sentences.zh: 年轻男子：是啊，真令人难以置信。

sentences.en: Like accountants
sentences.zh: 比如会计师。

sentences.en: You might think all the technological innovations would have put them out of a job, but in fact there are more of them than ever
sentences.zh: 你可能以为所有技术创新本该让他们失业，但事实上，如今会计师人数比以往任何时候都多。

sentences.en: They're still really in demand and have become far more efficient
sentences.zh: 他们依然需求旺盛，并且工作效率已大大提高。

sentences.en: YOUNG WOMAN: Right
sentences.zh: 年轻女子：对。

sentences.en: That was amazing
sentences.zh: 那真是令人惊叹。

sentences.en: Twenty times more accountants in this country compared to the 19th century
sentences.zh: 这个国家的会计师人数相比19世纪增加了二十倍。

sentences.en: YOUNG MAN: I know
sentences.zh: 年轻男子：我知道。

sentences.en: I'd never have thought that demand for hairdressing would have gone up so much in the last hundred years
sentences.zh: 我从未想到过去一百年间理发师的需求会上升得如此之多。

sentences.en: One hairdresser for every 287 people now, compared to one for over 1,500
sentences.zh: 如今每287人就拥有一名理发师，而过去则是每1500多人才有一名。

sentences.en: YOUNG WOMAN: Yeah because people's earning power has gone up so they can afford to spend more on personal services like that
sentences.zh: 年轻女子：是啊，因为人们的收入水平提高了，因而更有能力在理发等个人服务上增加支出。

sentences.en: YOUNG MAN: But technology hasn't changed the actual job that much
sentences.zh: 年轻男子：但技术其实并未大幅改变理发师这份工作的实质。

sentences.en: YOUNG WOMAN: No, they've got hairdryers, etc. but it's one job where you don't depend on a computer
sentences.zh: 年轻女子：没错，他们有了吹风机等设备，但这是一份你无需依赖电脑的工作……

sentences.en: The kind of work that administrative staff do has changed enormously, thanks to technology
sentences.zh: 得益于技术，行政人员所从事的工作类型已发生了巨大变化。

sentences.en: Even 20 years ago there were secretaries doing dictation and typing
sentences.zh: 甚至20年前，还有秘书从事听写和打字工作。

sentences.en: YOUNG MAN: Yes
sentences.zh: YOUNG MAN: 是的。

sentences.en: Really boring compared to these days, when they're given much more responsibility and higher status
sentences.zh: 与当今相比，这确实非常枯燥乏味；如今秘书被赋予了更多责任，地位也更高。

sentences.en: YOUNG WOMAN: Mmm
sentences.zh: YOUNG WOMAN: 嗯。

sentences.en: A lot of graduates go in for this kind of work now
sentences.zh: 如今许多毕业生都选择从事这类工作……

sentences.en: I'd expected there a to be a much bigger change in the number of agricultural workers in the 19th century
sentences.zh: 我原本预计19世纪农业工人的数量会发生更大变化。

sentences.en: But the 1871 census showed that roughly 25% of the population worked on the land
sentences.zh: 但1871年的人口普查显示，大约25%的人口从事农业劳动。

sentences.en: YOUNG MAN: Yeah, I'd have assumed it would be more than 50%
sentences.zh: YOUNG MAN: 是啊，我本以为会超过50%。

sentences.en: Now it's less than 0.2%
sentences.zh: 而如今这一比例已不足0.2%。

sentences.en: YOUNG WOMAN: What about care workers?
sentences.zh: YOUNG WOMAN: 那护理人员呢？

sentences.en: YOUNG MAN: They barely existed in the 19th century as people's lifespan was so much shorter
sentences.zh: YOUNG MAN: 19世纪几乎不存在护理人员，因为当时人们的寿命要短得多。

sentences.en: But now of course this sector will see huge growth
sentences.zh: 但如今，这一行业当然将迎来巨大增长。

sentences.en: YOUNG WOMAN: Yeah - and it's hard enough to meet current demand
sentences.zh: YOUNG WOMAN: 是啊——而且目前连现有需求都难以满足。

sentences.en: The future looks quite bleak for bank clerks
sentences.zh: 银行职员的未来看起来相当黯淡。

sentences.en: They've been in decline since ATMs were introduced in the eighties
sentences.zh: 自20世纪80年代自动取款机（ATM）问世以来，这一职业便持续衰落。

sentences.en: YOUNG MAN: And technology will certainly make most of the jobs they do now redundant, I think
sentences.zh: YOUNG MAN: 我认为，技术无疑将使他们目前所从事的大部分工作变得多余。

sentences.en: YOUNG WOMAN: I agree, although the situation may change
sentences.zh: YOUNG WOMAN: 我同意，尽管情况可能会发生变化。

sentences.en: It's very hard to predict what will happen
sentences.zh: 要预测未来会发生什么非常困难。
